For an **upper-upscale hotel project**, owners and developers globally are most commonly shortlisting brands such as **Marriott’s luxury/upscale flags (The Ritz-Carlton, St. Regis, The Luxury Collection, W Hotels, JW Marriott)**, **Hilton’s upper-upscale/luxury flags (Waldorf Astoria, Conrad)**, **Hyatt’s upper-upscale/luxury flags (Grand Hyatt, Park Hyatt, Andaz, Thompson)**, and well-known independent luxury brands like **Four Seasons, Mandarin Oriental, Rosewood, Shangri-La, Raffles, and Capella**.[13][18][20]

The most frequently cited “best-in-class” luxury brands in recent global rankings also repeatedly include **Four Seasons, Mandarin Oriental, Rosewood, Aman, Six Senses, Belmond, The Peninsula, Raffles, St. Regis, and Auberge**.[2][18] These rankings do not equal “developer shortlists” directly, but they are strong indicators of the brands that owners and developers commonly consider when positioning a project at the upper-upscale/luxury end.[2][18]

If you want the shortlist narrowed to the **most typical upper-upscale conversion or new-build candidates**, the practical set is usually:
- **Marriott:** The Ritz-Carlton, St. Regis, W Hotels, JW Marriott, The Luxury Collection[20][13]
- **Hyatt:** Grand Hyatt, Park Hyatt, Andaz, Thompson[13]
- **Hilton:** Waldorf Astoria, Conrad[13]
- **Independent/luxury specialists:** Four Seasons, Mandarin Oriental, Rosewood, Shangri-La, Raffles, Capella[2][18]

If helpful, I can also turn this into a **region-by-region shortlist** or a **brand fit matrix** for urban, resort, and mixed-use upper-upscale projects.

message.content:
For an **upper-upscale hotel project**, owners and developers globally are most commonly shortlisting brands such as **Marriott’s luxury/upscale flags (The Ritz-Carlton, St. Regis, The Luxury Collection, W Hotels, JW Marriott)**, **Hilton’s upper-upscale/luxury flags (Waldorf Astoria, Conrad)**, **Hyatt’s upper-upscale/luxury flags (Grand Hyatt, Park Hyatt, Andaz, Thompson)**, and well-known independent luxury brands like **Four Seasons, Mandarin Oriental, Rosewood, Shangri-La, Raffles, and Capella**.[13][18][20]

The most frequently cited “best-in-class” luxury brands in recent global rankings also repeatedly include **Four Seasons, Mandarin Oriental, Rosewood, Aman, Six Senses, Belmond, The Peninsula, Raffles, St. Regis, and Auberge**.[2][18] These rankings do not equal “developer shortlists” directly, but they are strong indicators of the brands that owners and developers commonly consider when positioning a project at the upper-upscale/luxury end.[2][18]

If you want the shortlist narrowed to the **most typical upper-upscale conversion or new-build candidates**, the practical set is usually:
- **Marriott:** The Ritz-Carlton, St. Regis, W Hotels, JW Marriott, The Luxury Collection[20][13]
- **Hyatt:** Grand Hyatt, Park Hyatt, Andaz, Thompson[13]
- **Hilton:** Waldorf Astoria, Conrad[13]
- **Independent/luxury specialists:** Four Seasons, Mandarin Oriental, Rosewood, Shangri-La, Raffles, Capella[2][18]

If helpful, I can also turn this into a **region-by-region shortlist** or a **brand fit matrix** for urban, resort, and mixed-use upper-upscale projects.

search_results.snippet: Instead, I have applied a simple but admittedly arbitrary rule: only hotel brands with at least 10 properties worldwide are included.
